title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter passed through a large S-shaped fold in the solar wind's magnetic field and measured the charged oxygen and carbon particles inside it. Their composition showed the plasma came from hot magnetic loops on the Sun, released when open and closed field lines reconnected. Waves and turbulence then appear to shape the fold as it travels outward, helping scientists understand how charged particles follow magnetic field lines and improving space weather forecasts.

title: Fastest star in the Milky Way feels the rotation of our central black hole
summary: The Milky Way’s massive black hole is rapidly rotating, and a star in an unprecedentedly close orbit could help measure its spin

title: Webb measures distance to farthest fast radio burst, suggesting origin
summary: Using the Webb telescope, astronomers located the host galaxy of FRB 20240304B, the most distant fast radio burst yet found, and measured its redshift as 2.148. The galaxy turned out to be a small, young dwarf that formed most of its stars quickly. This favours the idea that these brief radio flashes come from magnetars rather than from slow neutron star mergers, and the burst's signal also carried imprints of matter it passed through.

title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has imaged NGC 7129, a star-forming nebula about 3,300 light-years away, using infrared light that passes through dust which blocks visible light. Its brightest star, a pre-main-sequence star of 5 to 8 solar masses, is shrinking under gravity and heating up before hydrogen fusion begins. Outflows and radiation from young stars have carved a cavity spanning about 3.5 light-years, compressing gas that may form new stars.
